Chief Complaint
Increased thirst and nighttime urination for about 2 months.

History of Present Illness
66-year-old man presents for evaluation of polydipsia and nocturia (2-3 times per night) for approximately 2 months. Reports mild fatigue. No weight loss, chest pain, or vision changes. Home blood pressure readings have been 'around 150s' per patient. Fasting labs drawn this morning (see separate lab report).

Past Medical History
No prior chronic conditions on record. Appendectomy (1978).

Medications
None.

Allergies
Allergies: Sulfonamide (sulfa) antibiotics - rash.

Social / Family History
Retired civil engineer. Former smoker, quit 1995 (15 pack-years). Alcohol 2-3 drinks/week. Father had type 2 diabetes and stroke.

Vital Signs
BP 152/94 mmHg (repeat 148/92) | HR 78 regular | Temp 98.2 F | SpO2 97% RA | Height 175 cm | Weight 84 kg | BMI 27.4

Physical Exam
Well-appearing. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. Feet: intact sensation to monofilament, pulses palpable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus, newly diagnosed (HbA1c 8.4%, fasting glucose 168 mg/dL).
2. Essential hypertension.
3. Hyperlipidemia (LDL 142 mg/dL).

Plan
1. Start metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily with meals.
2. Start lisinopril 10 mg by mouth once daily.
3. Start atorvastatin 20 mg by mouth nightly.
4. Diabetes education referral; dietary counseling given.
5. Annual diabetic eye exam referral.
6. Repeat HbA1c and BMP in 3 months.

Riverside General Hospital
1200 Riverside Drive, Springfield, IL 62704 | Tel (217) 555-0140

Hospital Discharge Summary

Patient	SMITH, JOHN	MRN	4471-2093
DOB / Age	03/14/1956 (68 y)	Sex	Male
Date	09/19/2024	Attending	David Kim, MD (Hospitalist)

Admission: 09/15/2024 Discharge: 09/19/2024 Length of stay: 4 nights Disposition: Home

Principal Diagnosis
Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe.

Secondary Diagnoses
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia; essential hypertension; hyperlipidemia.

Allergies
Allergies: Sulfonamide (sulfa) antibiotics - rash.

Hospital Course
68-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presented with 3 days of fever (Tmax 38.9 C / 102.0 F), productive cough, and dyspnea. SpO2 91% on room air on arrival. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation. WBC 14.8, CRP 96. CURB-65 score 1; admitted for oxygen requirement.

Treated with ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and azithromycin 500 mg IV daily. Required 2 L nasal cannula oxygen for 48 hours, weaned to room air on hospital day 3. Afebrile since 09/17. Blood cultures negative.

Diabetes: Metformin was held on admission due to acute illness and IV contrast consideration; glucose managed with insulin lispro sliding scale (range 160-250 mg/dL). Metformin resumed at discharge. Lisinopril and atorvastatin continued throughout.

Condition at Discharge
Stable. SpO2 96% RA, Temp 98.4 F, BP 134/82, HR 84.

Discharge Medications
NEW: Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg by mouth twice daily x 5 days (last dose 09/24/2024)
RESUMED: Metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily
CONTINUE: Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth daily
CONTINUE: Atorvastatin 20 mg by mouth nightly
STOPPED: Insulin lispro sliding scale (inpatient only)

Follow-up
1. Primary care (Dr. Emily Carter) within 1-2 weeks.
2. Repeat chest X-ray in 4-6 weeks.
3. Return to ED for fever > 101 F, worsening shortness of breath, or chest pain.
4. Pneumococcal vaccine recommended once recovered.

Reason for Visit
Palpitations and fatigue for 1 week; referred by Dr. Emily Carter for irregular pulse.

History of Present Illness
69-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia; hospitalized 09/2024 for community-acquired pneumonia (resolved). Reports 1 week of intermittent palpitations, reduced exercise tolerance, and fatigue. No syncope, chest pain, or focal neurologic symptoms. ECG today shows atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response.

Current Medications (before this visit)
Metformin 500 mg twice daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; atorvastatin 20 mg nightly.

Allergies
Allergies: Sulfonamide (sulfa) antibiotics - rash.

Vital Signs
BP 138/86 mmHg | HR 118 irregularly irregular | SpO2 97% RA | Weight 82 kg

Data Reviewed
ECG: AF with RVR, rate 118. Echo: LVEF 55%, mildly dilated LA. Labs: TSH 2.1 (normal), hs-troponin 9 (normal), BNP 180, creatinine 1.18, eGFR 65, HbA1c 6.9%.

Assessment
1. Atrial fibrillation, new onset, rapid ventricular response, hemodynamically stable.
   CHA₂DS₂-VASc = 3 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1, diabetes = 1). HAS-BLED = 1.
2. Type 2 diabetes, improved control (HbA1c 8.4% in 2023 -> 6.9% now).
3. Hypertension.
4. Mildly reduced kidney function (eGFR 65, down from 74 in 2023).

Plan
1. Start apixaban 5 mg by mouth twice daily for stroke prevention (no dose-reduction criteria met: age < 80, weight > 60 kg, creatinine < 1.5).
2. Start metoprolol succinate 50 mg by mouth once daily for rate control.
3. Continue metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin.
4. Avoid NSAIDs while on anticoagulation.
5. Return in 4 weeks with repeat ECG; consider cardioversion if symptoms persist.
6. Recheck renal function in 3 months.
